newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq briefs Syrians on food needs.
newsitem.headline: Iraq briefs Syrians on food needs.

text.p: Iraqi Trade Minister Mohammad Mehdi Saleh has briefed Syrian businessmen on his country's food needs under Iraq's oil-for-food deal with the United Nations, the head of a visiting Syrian group of traders said on Tuesday.

"The minister reviewed Iraq's food needs in general," said Rateb al-Shallah, chairman of Syria's Chamber of Commerce and Industry, who arrived in Baghdad on Monday accompanied by six leading Syrian businessmen.
Shallah said he would not sign trade deals with Iraq at this stage.
The official Iraqi News Agency (INA) said Saleh discussed with the Syrians "the possibility of importing food and medicine from Syria which is allowed by the U.N. Security Council resolutions."

Under the deal, which went into effect in December, Iraq is permitted to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy urgent needs for Iraqis. The pact is exempted from the U.N. sanctions imposed on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Shallah also met on Tuesday Iraq's Industry and Minerals Minister Adnan Abdul-Majeed Jassim. "We have found our brothers as we have wished them," Shallah told Reuters. He gave no further details.

Syrian trade visit is the first since diplomatic ties between the two countries, ruled by rival factions of the Arab Baath party, were ruptured when Damascus sided with Iran in the 1980-1988 Iraq-Iran war.
